We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=j$ and $b=3\,i.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(j)+t(3\,i-j) \\  & =3t\,i+(1-t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3t\,y=1-t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\frac{1}{x+y}\,i+\frac{2y}{x+y}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{3t+1-t}\,i+\frac{2-2t}{3t+1-t}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2t+1}\,i+\frac{2-2t}{2t+1}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-t)j \\  & =3\,i-j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\frac{1}{2t+1}\,i+\frac{2-2t}{2t+1}\,j)\cdot (3\,i-j) \\  & =\frac{1}{2t+1}\cdot 3+\frac{2-2t}{2t+1}\cdot (-1) \\  & =\frac{3-2+2t}{2t+1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}1\,dt \\  & =t{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
